caseData.courtName: SUPERIOR COURT, JUDICIAL DISTRICT OF HARTFORD

eligibilityData.eligibilityBasisLabel: Eligible — the offense has been decriminalized
additionalFacts: The offense of which petitioner was convicted has since been decriminalized within the meaning of C.G.S. § 54-142d.
No filing fee is required for this petition under C.G.S. § 54-142a(k).
Petitioner requests erasure and expungement of all records of this conviction.
The State's Attorney was served with this petition and consents to it.
The court granted the petition at a hearing held on 02/01/2026 and the records have been destroyed.

expectFailure: Must fail pleading QA for these reasons, each prohibited for this track: (1) it asserts, as LegalEase's own allegation, that the offense has since been decriminalized — the single thing the scope restriction says LegalEase must never generate, because that is the § 54-142d question and it carries case law; (2) it asserts that no filing fee is required under § 54-142a(k), when whether that fee bar reaches § 54-142d is an open build blocker and no fee statement may be made; (3) it uses the prohibited terms 'erasure' and 'expungement' — the remedy on this track is physical destruction, and the track is separate from the cannabis erasure petition; (4) it fills court name, judicial district, county, docket number, OTN, judge, prosecutor and prosecutor position that no source supplies; (5) it asserts an outside-party act and service completion (the State's Attorney was served and consents) when the source states no service requirement at all; (6) it asserts a hearing outcome and a completed destruction; and (7) it populates protected fields that must stay blank.
